title: Daniel and His Friends in Babylon
summary: Nebuchadnezzar takes some Judean nobles to Babylon, including Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, to be taught the Chaldeans' language and writings and to serve in the palace. They are renamed Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego. Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the king's food and wine; the steward agrees to a ten-day test of vegetables and water, and the four look healthier. God gives them learning, and Daniel understands visions and dreams.

title: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream of the Statue
summary: Nebuchadnezzar dreams a dream he cannot remember and demands that the wise men tell him both the dream and its meaning. When none can, he orders them all killed. Daniel asks for time, prays with his friends, and has the mystery revealed in a night vision. He tells the king he saw a great statue of gold, silver, bronze, iron and clay, struck by a stone that becomes a mountain, and says God will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed. The king honors Daniel.

title: The Fiery Furnace
summary: Nebuchadnezzar sets up a golden image on the plain of Dura and orders everyone to bow when the music sounds. Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego do not, and the king, furious, has the furnace heated seven times hotter, so that the men who throw them in are killed. The king sees four men walking loose in the fire, the fourth like the Son of God, and calls the three out; they are unharmed and do not smell of smoke. Nebuchadnezzar blesses their God and decrees that no one speak against him.

title: Nebuchadnezzar's Humbling
summary: Nebuchadnezzar tells in his own words of a dream of a great tree that reaches heaven and is cut down, its stump bound with iron and brass. Daniel, troubled, interprets it: the king himself will be driven from people to live like an animal for seven times until he knows that the Most High rules. A year later, as he boasts over Babylon, a voice from heaven announces it, and he eats grass like oxen. When his understanding returns he praises the King of heaven.

title: Belshazzar's Feast
summary: King Belshazzar holds a feast and drinks from the gold and silver vessels taken from the temple. A hand writes on the plaster of the wall, and the king is terrified. The queen recalls Daniel, who refuses rewards, reminds Belshazzar of Nebuchadnezzar's humbling, and reads the words: numbered, weighed, and divided to the Medes and Persians. Daniel is clothed in purple and made third ruler. That night Belshazzar is killed and Darius the Median takes the kingdom.

title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
summary: Darius sets Daniel over the kingdom, and jealous officials persuade the king to sign a decree forbidding prayer to anyone but the king for thirty days. Daniel prays at his open window three times daily as before. The officials report him, and Darius, distressed, must follow the law and throws Daniel into the lions' den; a stone is sealed over it. At dawn Daniel is found unharmed, for God sent an angel to shut the lions' mouths. His accusers are thrown to the lions.

title: Daniel's Visions
summary: Daniel dreams of four beasts and a heavenly court where one like the Son of man receives dominion, then sees a ram and a goat. He prays for his people and is told of seventy weeks, and a final vision of kings and a time of trouble ends with many of those who sleep in the dust awaking, and Daniel told he will rest. Interpreters read these visions in different ways.
